problem: VLN/end-to-end navigation policies lack geospatial grounding for long-range outdoor missions. OSM-based methods (e.g. OpenBench/OPEN) depend on cloud LLMs that hallucinate and add latency, and cannot do open-vocabulary last-mile object search.
motivation: Outdoor ground robots must combine long-distance route following with fine-grained semantic search near the goal (e.g. 'go to the library and find the person in red'). This has to run offline on edge hardware, so hallucination-free grounding to real map entities and local deployment are needed.
key_idea: Ground language to OSM entities via zero-shot Trie-constrained generative retrieval with a local LLM, plan via LLM-generated Behavior Trees and OSRM routes, then switch to frontier exploration with an open-set semantic voxel map (RayFronts) for last-mile search.
insight: Constrained decoding over a Trie of valid entity IDs guarantees valid outputs: GeoQA beats GPT-4o on the Easy split (R@1 97.6 vs 96.7) and clearly beats the unconstrained Qwen2.5-14B on Hard (74.8 vs 67.7). GPT-4o still wins on Hard (87.4). The real-robot ablation shows the topological guidance from RAPPER is decisive: without it SPL is 0 in 3 of 4 trials. Compared with OPEN, the 3D voxel semantic map preserves distant targets that its flat 2D BEV projection loses.
method: GeoQA: builds hierarchical IDs ('Category-Name') for OSM entities and a prefix Trie. One local LLM is called twice: a CoT pass extracts target category and modifiers, then Trie-constrained beam search decodes a valid entity ID and its coordinates.

RAPPER: Qwen2.5-14B local LLM parses instructions into nav/explore sub-tasks and synthesizes an XML Behavior Tree (ProgPrompt-style) from a skill pool (GlobalPlanning, FollowPath, Exploration). BT ticks trigger recovery when the robot is stuck.
Global planning: the goal is the nearest point on the target polygon contour, not the centroid. OSRM on local OSM produces the global topological route.

Heading initialization and waypoint sampling: a 5 m straight drive with GPS gives the bias angle between the GPS/ENU frame and odometry, transforming global waypoints to the local frame. Curvature-adaptive sampling uses 3 m at turns and 20 m on straights.

NæVIS last-mile exploration: LIO plus RGB-D feed the RayFronts open-set semantic voxel map. Near the goal the robot does a 360° scan, then Yamauchi frontier exploration filtered by point-in-polygon against the OSM boundary. Voxels above a similarity threshold are clustered with DBSCAN and the dominant centroid becomes the goal.
Local deployment: everything runs offline on edge hardware (Jetson AGX Orin). Only the initial BT requires a link to an edge server.

setting.backbone: Qwen2.5-14B (frozen, local; used for both GeoQA and RAPPER) + RayFronts open-vocabulary encoder
setting.action_space: OSM/OSRM global waypoints followed by local-planner trajectories (FAR-planner-style); frontier goals for exploration
setting.simulator: NVIDIA Isaac Sim (campus digital twins from OSM), Nova Carter UGV
setting.privileged: none at test (OSM map is a prior); baseline OPEN was given exact coordinates and NoMaD target images

numbers.eval_set_note: 45 episodes (5 buildings x 3 positions x 3 yaws); building-goal navigation, success within 5 m
numbers.extra: OSM prior; baselines given exact coords / target images

numbers.eval_set_note: 45 episodes; navigation plus last-mile object search, success within 2 m

numbers_note: Custom benchmarks only; no standard benchmarks. Splits are labeled 'test' by convention. Table 3 gives per-trial SPL only.
results: In Isaac Sim campus tasks, G-DRAGON reaches 100% SR (300m) and 95.56% (800m) on Task 1, versus OPEN 77.78/26.67 and NoMaD 33.33/0. On Task 2 it gets 62.22% SR at 800m vs OPEN 17.78%. GeoQA beats BM25, DPR and vanilla Qwen2.5-14B, beats GPT-4o on Easy, and trails it on Hard. It is the only method to finish all four real-world trials.
limitations: Initial Behavior Tree generation still needs a network link to a local edge server, so mission start needs network coverage.
Evaluation is small (45 episodes per setting, 4 real trials) on custom campus benchmarks, and GeoQA lags GPT-4o on implicit/Hard queries (74.8 vs 87.4 R@1).
Baselines were only NoMaD and OPEN, given privileged inputs (exact coordinates, target images); the geospatial dataset is LLM-synthesized and uses a single campus.
